newsitem.title: USA: Christopher meets top Israelis, Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Christopher meets top Israelis, Palestinians.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher called in top Israeli and Palestinian officials on Wednesday to thrash out key issues dividing them as an emergency Middle East summit went into its second day.

State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said Christopher was meeting with Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy and foreign policy adviser Dore Gold and Palestinian negotiators Nabil Shaath and Yasser Abed Rabbo.
"The secretary (of state) thought it would be a good idea to get the Israelis and Palestinians to assess where they are," Burns said. "All major issues are on the table."

Christopher's talks followed almost all-night discussions between U.S. Middle East coordinator Dennis Ross and Israeli and Palestinian officials at Blair House, a U.S. government residence opposite the White House. U.S. officials said Ross left the meeting at 5 a.m. (0900 GMT).

"As a result of the discussions overnight, these talks are at a very intensive stage. But very serious issues remain. There is a lot of hard work ahead today but the Secretary is determined to push forward," Burns said.

Tuesday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat met alone after U.S. President Bill Clinton called the summit in a bid to prevent a collapse of the peace process following bloody clashes in the West Bank and Gaza Strip last week.
